result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.betweenness_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate betweenness centrality scores for all nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L14474-L14583){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.betweenness_centrality(attr_name=None, return_dict=False) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Betweenness centrality measures how often a node appears on the shortest paths between other nodes in the graph. Nodes with high betweenness act as bridges or bottlenecks, controlling the flow of information or resources through the network. This metric is particularly useful for: - identifying key connectors in social networks - finding critical infrastructure nodes in transportation/communication networks - detecting potential bottlenecks or points of failure The algorithm computes shortest paths between all pairs of nodes and counts how many times each node appears on these paths. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name to store betweenness scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), automatically uses `betweenness_centrality`. Overwrites column if it already exists. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns a dictionary instead of self. If `False` (default), stores in NDF and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to betweenness scores (range of `[0, 1]`). If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Find bridge nodes in a network: ::: {#828a6311 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec # Create two clusters connected by a bridge node graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="Bridge") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_edge("A", "B") .add_edge("B", "Bridge") .add_edge("Bridge", "C") .add_edge("C", "D") ) scores = graph.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) bridge_id = graph.get_id_from_label("Bridge") # High score - Bridge node bridges two clusters scores[bridge_id] # Convert to labels if needed label_scores = {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): score for nid, score in scores.items()} # Same result accessed by label label_scores["Bridge"] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 0.6666666666666666 ``` ::: ::: Identify the most important connectors: ::: {#02e35dd3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_node(label="D") .add_node(label="E") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") .add_edge(source="B", target="C") .add_edge(source="C", target="D") .add_edge(source="D", target="E") ) scores = graph.betweenness_centrality(return_dict=True) # Get top 3 connectors by betweenness score connectors = sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:3] # Returns list of (node_id, score) tuples for top connectors connectors ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [(3, 0.6666666666666666), (4, 0.5), (2, 0.5)] ``` ::: :::
